title: You deleted the API key. Git didn't.

lines: You deleted the API key. Git didn't.
Real test. I committed a fake AWS key to this project, then removed it a few commits later.
The file is gone. It's not in the folder, and cat can't find it.
But Git stores every version of every file. One search finds the exact commit.
One more command, and the key is back. In under six milliseconds.
Secret scanners, good and bad, run a pattern search just like this, across every commit.
One. Revoke and rotate the key first. That's GitHub's own advice.
Two. Rewrite history with git filter-repo. But clones and forks can still keep copies.
Three. Turn on push protection, so secrets get blocked before they land.
And on AWS, prefer short-lived credentials, like IAM roles.
